pr_title: Fixes the normals of SphereMesh when the radius is different from 1
pr_body:
Fixes https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/52965.

The issue was that there was a "typo" in the previous code. The wrong coordinates were being multiplied by the radius. I didn't see it last time because I only tested the mesh for radius == 1. 

I have tested it now for varying values of "radius" and "height" when creating the sphere mesh, and compared the results with applying a transform to the whole mesh, so everything should be working now.

*Bugsquad edit: Redone version of https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/51995.*

issue_context.title: Wrong SphereMesh shading in 3.4 beta 5
issue_context.body: ### Godot version 3.4 beta 5 ### System information MacOS M1 ### Issue description The default shading seems to be broken. The shading in beta 5 looks as if the light comes from the top, even though the directional light comes from the upper left in the screenshots. The issue does not occur in Beta 4 ### 3.4 Beta 5 ### 3.3 Stable ### Steps to reproduce Create a scene with a mesh and a directional light. ### Minimal reproduction project [ExpeditionSim.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/7216207/ExpeditionSim.zip)

review_comments: Probably a dumb question but why is it `* scale` on `x` and `z`, and `/ scale` on `y`?

scale is basically just the "vertical radius", so you can think of a the ellipsoid as a unit sphere scaled by "scale" in the y axis and by "radius" in the x and z axis.

Because of this, the normal actually needs to be scaled in the x and z axis by `scale`, and in the y axis by `radius`. This is a particular case of using the transpose of the inverse of the transform matrix, which one usually does when transforming normals. See my explanation in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/51995.

The `/scale` factor on `y` comes from the fact that `y`is already scaled vertically  (since `y = scale * cos(Math_PI * v);`), so by dividing by scale we get `cos(Math_PI*v)`

To sum up:
If `(x,y,z)` is a point in the unit sphere, the (not normalized) normal of the scaled ellipsoid is given by:
`normal = (x*scale,y*radius,z*scale)`
